# Objective

Generate an interactive map of france to visualize the evolution of the population density over the year and the economic growth of the region and some others social socio-economical indicators.

# Planning

- Define where to extract information to plot the map, maybe `geo.api.gouv.fr`
- Define to use R or python to plot the interactive map
- Define where to extract the information of the population (or population density)
- Show information as tooltip, make filters to be show in bar plots `geom_col`
- Look for the possibility of integrate this data with google maps or some other popular map.


# Development

```{python}
import json
import urllib.request

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

# GeoJSON of French regions (simplified), includes overseas regions
GEOJSON_URL = (
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gregoiredavid/france-geojson/"
    "master/regions-version-simplifiee.geojson"
)

with urllib.request.urlopen(GEOJSON_URL) as response:
    geojson = json.load(response)

# Approximate data (INSEE, ~2021): code, name, population, area in km²
data = [
    ("11", "Île-de-France",            12_270_000, 12_012),
    ("24", "Centre-Val de Loire",       2_570_000, 39_151),
    ("27", "Bourgogne-Franche-Comté",   2_810_000, 47_784),
    ("28", "Normandie",                 3_320_000, 29_906),
    ("32", "Hauts-de-France",           6_000_000, 31_806),
    ("44", "Grand Est",                 5_560_000, 57_441),
    ("52", "Pays de la Loire",          3_850_000, 32_082),
    ("53", "Bretagne",                  3_370_000, 27_208),
    ("75", "Nouvelle-Aquitaine",        6_150_000, 84_036),
    ("76", "Occitanie",                 5_930_000, 72_724),
    ("84", "Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes",      8_070_000, 69_711),
    ("93", "Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur", 5_100_000, 31_400),
    ("94", "Corse",                       350_000,  8_680),
]
df = pd.DataFrame(data, columns=["code", "region", "population", "area_km2"])
df["density"] = (df["population"] / df["area_km2"]).round(1)

# Keep only metropolitan regions (drops overseas ones from the GeoJSON)
metro_codes = set(df["code"])
geojson["features"] = [
    f for f in geojson["features"] if f["properties"]["code"] in metro_codes
]

fig = px.choropleth(
    df,
    geojson=geojson,
    locations="code",
    featureidkey="properties.code",
    color="density",
    hover_name="region",
    hover_data={"code": False, "population": ":,", "density": ":.1f"},
    color_continuous_scale="YlOrRd",
    labels={"density": "Density (inhab./km²)"},
    title="Population density by region – Metropolitan France",
)
fig.update_geos(fitbounds="locations", visible=False)
fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=0, r=0, t=50, b=0))
fig.show()

```
